Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D status was not associated with depression symptoms (CDI score of 19 or more), whether fitted continuously or categorically.
Sentence: "There was no significant association between 25(OH)D and depression symptoms whether 25(OH)D was fitted as a continuous variable (crude odds ratio (OR) 0 .99 [95%CI: 0.98, 1.01], p = 0.458 and adjusted OR 1.01 [95%CI: 0.99, 1.02], p = 0.233), categorical variable as per acceptable cut-of points (crude analysis p = 0.376 and adjusted analysis p = 0.736), or categorical variable as quartiles (crude analysis p = 0.760 and adjusted analysis p = 0.549)."
Measured as: depression symptoms (CDI score of 19 or more)
Population: 704 randomly selected adolescents in middle schools in Kuwait
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Different vitamin D levels/status
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 704
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Genetically predicted higher serum 25(OH)D levels were causally associated with lower odds of depression in Mendelian randomization.
Sentence: "The MR analysis, utilizing 32 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) as instrumental variables, revealed a significant causal association between 25(OH)D levels and depression, with all MR methods (excluding Simple Mode) yielding p-values < 0.05."
Measured as: depression
Population: Genetic summary statistics from GWAS datasets (IEU Open GWAS Project) for 25(OH)D levels and depression
Intervention: Genetically predicted serum 25(OH)D levels (32 SNPs as instruments)
Comparator: Lower genetically predicted 25(OH)D levels
Design: other primary study
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both findings bear on vitamin D and depression; the cross-sectional null and the Mendelian randomization benefit differ mainly in design, a genetic proxy against measured level in a different population.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"design_or_bias","also_differs":["population"],"detail":"design: cross-sectional measured 25(OH)D in Kuwaiti adolescents vs Mendelian randomization of genetically predicted 25(OH)D in GWAS summary statistics"}
